I will do it mostly the way I have done it before, because changing too much is risky. I have 15 mu total, and on my land the wheat and maize go one after the other, so I will keep most of the ground in the wheat-maize run and leave a smaller piece for cotton. I will put 10 mu into winter wheat, then after wheat harvest I will sow summer maize on those same 10 mu. The other 5 mu I will keep for cotton. I do not like to cut fertilizer too hard. If I save a little money on fertilizer and the crop turns weak, that loss is bigger than wasting one extra bag. I also look at what people around me do. Around here, if wheat wants a decent head, I will feed it heavier than cotton. Maize also needs a good mouthful, especially if I want a full ear. Cotton I will not starve either, but I will not spend on it like wheat. Since I have well water, I will irrigate when the crop really needs it and not wait for the sky. For tillage, I will keep it simple: rotary for wheat and maize after harvest work, and plough the cotton ground before planting so the soil loosens deeper. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen it work in other people’s fields, but I will still manage it in the old steady way.
